channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Achieves Record Cotton Harvest of Over Five Million Tons
item.description: Uzbekistan has harvested over five million tons of raw cotton in 2026, a record since its independence in 1991. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attributed this success to increased yields and mechanization, despite reduced planting areas. Farmers are expected to profit significantly.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Energy Efficiency as Investment in Sustainable Future
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing energy efficiency for the autumn-winter period, focusing on heat conservation and rational resource use. Uzpsb Bank reported its "green" credit portfolio exceeded $730 million by October 1, 2026, representing 15% of its total portfolio. These funds support solar energy, energy-efficient construction materials, and infrastructure development.

item.title: Illegal Call Center Discovered in Tashkent, 23 Foreign Nationals Found
item.description: An illegal call center operating from a private residence in Tashkent's Yakkasaroy district has been uncovered by the Ministry of Internal Affairs. During a raid, 23 foreign nationals residing in Uzbekistan without proper permits were found. Authorities also seized electronic devices and passports.

item.title: Uzbek President Arrives in Astana for Central Asia Security Summit
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan has arrived in Astana, Kazakhstan, at the invitation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and King Abdullah II of Jordan. He will attend a summit of Central Asian leaders focused on artificial intelligence security and countering its misuse for terrorism.

item.title: Kazakh Companies Sign Deals Worth $100 Million at China International Import Expo
item.description: Kazakh companies have signed agreements totaling approximately $100 million at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai. Kazakhstan's Minister of Trade and Integration, Arman Shakkaliyev, participated in the event, which aims to expand export opportunities and attract investment. The expo is a major platform for international trade.

item.title: Yandex Lavka plans to launch robot deliveries in Tashkent by end of 2026
item.description: Yandex Uzbekistan plans to introduce autonomous robot deliveries for products, ready-made meals, and daily necessities through Yandex Lavka in Tashkent by the end of 2026. The company is currently testing the robots and preparing them for urban operation. Robots will navigate independently, using lidar and ultrasonic sensors, and can handle curbs up to 10 cm high, operating even in rain.

item.title: Uzbekistan reforms 'Women's Notebook' fund for enhanced support mechanisms
item.description: Uzbekistan has updated the 'Women's Notebook' fund mechanisms to provide new forms of assistance to women in need. Reforms include improved medical services, with up to 22 million soms for non-surgical treatment and 4.4 million soms for diagnostic tests. Housing repair assistance remains at 22 million soms, and rental subsidies have increased for women in various regions.

item.title: Armenia begins design work on US-backed trade corridor despite pending agreement
item.description: Armenian officials have started design work for the TRIPP trade corridor, a project announced with the United States in January. While a preliminary agreement outlined ownership, operational details are still pending. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that preparatory work will commence immediately, even before the official incorporation of TRIPP Development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Recovers $36 Million from Specialists Who Left Rural Jobs Early
item.description: In Kazakhstan's West Kazakhstan region, prosecutors are recovering 36 million tenge from young specialists who received state support for rural work but did not complete their mandatory five-year service. Courts have ruled in favor of the prosecution, and enforcement documents have been sent to bailiffs.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Arrives in Astana for Regional Security Summit
item.description: Turkmenistan President Serdar Berdymukhamedov has arrived in Astana to attend a summit on regional security. The meeting, part of the Aqaba Process initiated in 2015, focuses on joint efforts against terrorism and extremism. The summit is scheduled for November 6th.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Expanding Crime Prevention Bodies to Include Key Ministries
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering expanding its crime prevention system by adding entities like the Ministry of Emergency Situations, Ministry of Digital Technologies, and the Central Bank. A draft law proposes increasing prevention subjects from 14 to 21, with defined rights and obligations based on legislation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Implements New Order and Strict Control Over Drug Prices
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced a new mechanism for regulating and controlling drug prices, effective April 1, 2025. A presidential decree aims to prevent unjustified price increases, reduce public spending on medicines, and foster a transparent market. A reference pricing system will set maximum wholesale and retail markups.

item.title: Melania Trump Delivers Letters for Putin and Zelensky at White House Meeting
item.description: First Lady Melania Trump met with Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House to discuss humanitarian efforts in Oleshky, Ukraine. She conveyed letters to Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky, urging continued dialogue for civilian aid. The meeting focused on humanitarian operations.

item.title: Mayan Civilization's Decline Potentially Linked to Mercury Pollution from Red Pigments, Study Suggests
item.description: An international team of paleochemists has found evidence suggesting the Maya civilization's widespread use of mercury-based red pigments led to significant environmental and water contamination. This pollution may have contributed to the decline of major Maya urban centers between 250 and 950 AD, adding to previously identified causes like drought and conflict.

item.title: Calls for Stronger Joint Action Against Terrorism Discussed on Tahawol Program
item.description: The Tahawol program featured discussions on the need for enhanced joint efforts to combat terrorism. The segment also briefly touched upon unrelated sports news concerning Afghanistan's cricket and futsal teams, as well as a report on a Turkish Daesh suspect's arrival in Pakistan and Trump's comments on the Afghanistan war.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Fund Private Veterinarians from State Budget
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kyrgyzstan intends to pay salaries to private veterinarians from the state budget. This initiative, driven by a presidential directive, aims to improve veterinary service quality and stabilize the epidemiological situation. It also seeks to ensure the effective completion of state tasks, including animal identification.

item.title: Kazakhstan Initiates Civil Code Modernization to Meet New Economic Demands
item.description: Kazakhstan is modernizing its Civil Code to align with contemporary economic realities, including digital technologies and artificial intelligence. The initiative focuses on updating outdated regulations while preserving effective existing norms. The current code, adopted in 1994, requires revision due to significant economic shifts and new legal demands.

item.title: US and Turkmenistan Deepen Economic and Diplomatic Ties with Envoy Visit
item.description: The United States and Turkmenistan are strengthening their economic and diplomatic relationship, marked by a visit from a top U.S. diplomat and a business delegation to Ashgabat. Discussions focused on expanding business ties, identifying new partnership opportunities, and U.S. support for the TAPI gas pipeline.

item.title: Kurultai Adopts Six Laws in October, Two Signed by President
item.description: The Kurultai adopted six laws in October, with two of them receiving presidential assent. Currently, 41 draft laws are under review. Deputies issued 27 parliamentary inquiries, and the Public Reception of the Kurultai received 271 citizens. Legislative work and international cooperation continue.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Increase Private Sector Role in Healthcare Services
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing healthcare reforms, focusing on market mechanisms and international standards. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed plans to attract investment and expand private sector participation in healthcare. Master plans for the entire republic are to be completed by year-end, with a focus on infrastructure and outsourcing.

item.title: OSCE to Assess Feasibility of Sending Observers to Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: The OSCE's Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) is evaluating the possibility of sending an international observation mission to Kyrgyzstan's upcoming presidential election. The Central Election Commission met with ODIHR advisors to discuss preparations, including equipment testing, voter identification, and accessibility for people with disabilities.

item.title: South Korea to Expand Maritime Mission Area Towards Strait of Hormuz
item.description: South Korea plans to expand the operational area of its anti-piracy unit, Cheonghae, from the Gulf of Aden to international waters south of Oman. The mission radius will nearly double, with an additional patrol aircraft and specialized teams. The expansion aims to protect citizens and trade, with a non-combat focus.

item.title: Central Asian Leaders to Meet in Astana for Aqaba Process on AI Security
item.description: Leaders from Central Asian countries will convene in Astana on November 5-6 for a meeting within the Aqaba Process framework, focusing on artificial intelligence security and combating its use for terrorism and extremism. The initiative, launched in 2015, aims to strengthen international cooperation and coordinate security efforts against transnational threats.

item.title: Director Sentenced to Eight Years for Embezzling Social Housing Funds
item.description: A construction company director in Kazakhstan's Akmola region was sentenced to eight years and six months for embezzling 211 million tenge from state contracts for social housing. The funds were intended for two residential buildings. The director allegedly used the money for personal needs and debts.

item.title: Kazakh Court Orders National Companies to Compensate Woman Injured by Falling Roof
item.description: A Kazakh court has ordered Kazpost and Kazakhtelecom to jointly compensate a woman who was severely injured when a roof collapsed on her in May 2023. The companies must cover her medical expenses and provide lifelong monthly payments until she reaches retirement age.

item.title: Shymkent's "Zhuldyz" Industrial Zone Now Served by Railway Infrastructure
item.description: The construction of a dedicated railway line for the "Zhuldyz" industrial zone in Shymkent has been completed. The 6.4-kilometer line will facilitate the delivery of raw materials and finished products, enhancing the zone's logistical capabilities and attractiveness to investors.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizen Awarded Order of Friendship by Russian President Putin
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin presented the Order of Friendship to a Kyrgyz citizen, Zukhra Shidakova. Meanwhile, Kyrgyzstan's Interior Minister spoke at an international conference in Astana on combating cybercrime, noting an increase in AI-related fraud threats. A fire occurred at an ethno-complex in Alamedin district, destroying part of a kitchen and a yurt. Former traffic police chief Talantbek Isaev was fined for illegal parking in Tokmok. The resort town of Cholpon-A is undergoing reconstruction, with its mayor discussing its past and future development. President Sapar Japarov instructed the cabinet to consider banning energy drink production and imports within a month. Kyrgyz participants were recognized as best media specialists at the International Space Games.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Deputy Chairman: Key Rate May Decrease Below 10% in Three Years
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Deputy Chairman, Nodirbek Ochilov, stated that the key rate may be gradually reduced below 10% within the next three years. This process will primarily depend on inflation falling to the target level. Further details are available through the provided link.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine Exchange Drone Attacks; China Discusses Mediation
item.description: Russia and Ukraine engaged in continuous drone attacks over the past day. Russia claimed to have shot down 496 Ukrainian drones, while Ukraine reported destroying 105 out of 128 Russian drones. Ukrainian President Zelensky is discussing security guarantees with Western nations and preparing for trilateral talks with the US and Russia. China confirmed discussions with Moscow and Washington regarding a potential summit.

item.title: Presidents of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan Arrive in Astana for Aqaba Process Summit
item.description: The Presidents of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan have arrived in Astana to participate in the Aqaba Process Summit. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon was welcomed by Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev also arrived for the summit, which aims to strengthen international cooperation in combating terrorism, extremism, and transnational crime. Earlier, President Tokayev met with Jordan's King Abdullah II, and both leaders exchanged state awards.

item.title: 19 European Flights Received Bomb Threat Messages in 24 Hours
item.description: Nineteen flights across Europe received bomb threat messages within a 24-hour period, according to The Guardian. Flights between 14 countries, including France, Spain, and the UK, were affected. While all landed aircraft were cleared, the EU is investigating potential coordinated actions and monitoring the situation closely.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Police shoot tires of fleeing vehicle driven by minor
item.description: In Almaty region, police fired at the tires of a fleeing vehicle driven by an underage driver without a license. The minor endangered road users and attempted to evade authorities. The driver was apprehended, and his father faces administrative responsibility for neglecting parental duties. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Citizenship for 255 Individuals, Reduces Exits
item.description: Kazakhstan's citizenship commission recommended granting citizenship to 255 people and approving the renunciation of citizenship for 43 others. Vice President Yerlan Karin noted a declining trend in citizenship renunciation applications over the past eight years, attributing it to increased social optimism and the growing attractiveness of Kazakhstan's passport. The country's passport is considered the strongest in the region.

item.title: Shymkent blogger known as 'Askо' sentenced to 4.5 years for extortion
item.description: A blogger from Shymkent, known online as 'Askо', and two accomplices have been sentenced to 4.5 years in prison for extorting businessmen and officials. The group filmed videos potentially damaging to reputations and demanded money to suppress them.

item.title: Former MP urges EU to recognize Taliban's gender apartheid and designate them terrorists
item.description: Former Afghan MP Baktash Siawash addressed the European Parliament, urging the EU to formally recognize the Taliban's "gender apartheid" in Afghanistan. He called for an end to normalizing relations with the Taliban and requested they be designated a terrorist organization, criticizing European governments' diplomatic engagement with the group.

item.title: Latvia and Lithuania Consider Deploying Nuclear Weapons Amid Russian Threats
item.description: Latvia and Lithuania are exploring options to strengthen their security in light of Russia's nuclear threats. While initial political steps have been taken, deploying nuclear weapons requires agreement with allies and significant domestic preparations. The possibility of such deployment is being discussed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Easing of Auto and Housing Loan Regulations
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank will extend the easing of debt burden limits for certain auto loans by one year and for housing loans within the Zhilstroysberezheniya system by two years, until the end of 2029. This aims to support the stability of these lending segments.

item.title: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Welcomes Emomali Rahmon on Official Visit to Astana
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Kazakhstan for an official visit, where he was welcomed at Astana airport by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The visit, scheduled from November 5-7, will focus on strengthening strategic partnership and discussing cooperation in trade, economy, and other sectors.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Arrives in Astana for Akaba Process Summit
item.description: The President of Turkmenistan, Serdar Berdymukhamedov, has arrived in Astana to participate in the Akaba Process summit. This initiative focuses on coordinating security efforts and combating terrorism. The summit aims to foster cooperation among participating nations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Establish Integrated Agro-Food Park with EDB Support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will establish an integrated agro-food park following a trilateral agreement signed at the Regional Industrial Development Forum. The Eurasian Development Bank will provide $370,509 in financing, with participation from UNIDO. The project aims to develop agricultural processing and attract investments.
